issues.quote: Improved the performance of the main web app
issues.problem: Five years of experience reduced to four vague bullets with no stack, no metric and no scope. I can't tell what was slow, what was changed (bundle splitting, memoisation, image handling, caching) or what the result was. 'Responsible for the frontend of several client projects' says nothing about size, team or difficulty. 'Helped the juniors' is filler. Against a pile of CVs that quote Lighthouse scores, load times and conversion changes, this reads as someone who can't show what they did.
issues.fix: Rewrite each bullet as action, tool and result, e.g. 'Cut LCP on the main web app from 4.1s to 1.9s by code-splitting routes and lazy-loading images (React, Vite)'. Name the client types, team size, your part in the design system (components built, adoption, Storybook, a11y) and how you mentored the juniors (code reviews, pairing). If you don't have exact numbers, give honest approximate ones.

issues.problem: A date of birth breaks Belgian CV convention and gives the reader nothing job-relevant. Together with the language line ('Dutch: native · English: very good · French: basic'), which has no CEFR levels, it shows the CV wasn't adapted to the Belgian market, where employers expect Dutch, French and English on the A1-C2 scale.
issues.fix: Remove the date of birth. Change the languages line to CEFR levels, e.g. 'Dutch: C2 · English: C1 · French: A2'. Keep to one A4 page.

issues.problem: Self-rated dot scales tell a senior reader nothing and can hurt. A 3/5 for TypeScript on a frontend CV, next to a 5/5 for 'CSS / Sass', suggests this person is still weak in the language most React teams now require. Parsers drop the dot glyphs and the table, so the level information is lost anyway. The list also leaves out testing (Jest, Testing Library, Cypress or Playwright), Git, build tooling, accessibility and any named framework or router. The Vue internship and WordPress freelance work aren't connected to it.
issues.fix: Drop the dot ratings and the table. Use a plain grouped list, e.g. 'Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, CSS/Sass. Frameworks: React, Vue. Tooling: Vite, Git, Jest/Testing Library, Storybook.' Put each skill inside a bullet where you used it. Be ready to show real TypeScript work, or leave out the weak rating.

strength.quote: Worked on a React design system used by the whole team
strength.why: A shared design system is real frontend scope: component API design, reuse and consistency across projects. It is the one line that points to craft beyond building pages. It still needs detail on the stack, what the candidate built and how widely it was adopted.
